# typed-sql 2.0.0

typed-sql 2.0 turns the typed-query foundation into a production SQL compiler while preserving
the central contract: write SQL, install only the grammar and driver you use, and fail closed when
a query cannot be proved.

## Highlights

- Grammar-neutral query semantics describe operation, dependencies, cardinality, volatility,
  locking, connection affinity, and required adapter capabilities.
- Application-owned adapters add cardinality methods, cancellation and deadlines, prepared
  execution, transactions, batches, streams, routing, retries, and native bulk transfer without
  adding database drivers to grammar dependencies.
- Deterministic query manifests connect compiler evidence to live verification, query-plan
  governance, migration compatibility, routing, and redacted runtime observability.
- Result validation accepts the Standard Schema V1 interface, so applications can keep their
  preferred compatible validator, including exact-optional Zod and Valibot schemas without wrappers.
- The public conformance package gives third-party grammars executable inference, capability,
  fail-closed, runtime-adapter, codec, and performance contracts.

## Upgrade and compatibility

Read the [v1 to v2 upgrade contract](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/upgrading-from-v1)
before changing a grammar or custom adapter. The
[compatibility reference](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility) records the
supported and exactly tested environments.

The stable packages support Node.js 22.11 or newer. The compiler correctness path uses TypeScript
7.0.2. PostgreSQL and MySQL are stable dialect packages; their optional adapters use
application-installed `pg` and `mysql2`, respectively.

The following packages publish on the stable train:

- `@typed-sql/core`
- `@typed-sql/opentelemetry`
- `@typed-sql/ast`
- `@typed-sql/schema`
- `@typed-sql/config`
- `@typed-sql/compiler`
- `@typed-sql/conformance`
- `@typed-sql/postgres`
- `@typed-sql/mysql`
- `@typed-sql/cli`

`@typed-sql/ts-bridge`, `@typed-sql/language-server`, `@typed-sql/sqlite`, and the editor
integrations remain experimental. They stay on the `next` npm tag and are not dependencies of the
stable packages. SQLite uses `node:sqlite`; the preview TypeScript and editor integration remains
isolated from the stable compiler path.

## Evidence

The stable transition was rehearsed from `2.0.0-rc.1` in a clean worktree. The rehearsal ran the
repository verification suite, real packed-consumer PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite acceptance,
packed the ten-package stable train, and installed that train without any experimental package or
implicit database driver. It performed no registry writes and created no public tags. The protected
release workflow repeats those checks against the exact commit before publication and verifies the
published packages from npm afterward.

The release decision and workflow evidence are tracked in
[GitHub issue #81](https://github.com/Lojhan/typed-sql/issues/81).
